title: Removing DOISST v2.1 mean steps cuts the 2023/24 record SST jump from 0.25 to 0.19 C, its return period from about 500 to 110-160 years, and 1982-2025 heatwave-day trends by about a quarter (60S-60N)
abstract: Question: which published record-heat and marine heatwave (MHW) results from NOAA Daily OISST v2.1 (DOISST) survive when its mean steps (1985, 2005, 7 July 2020, 2021) and fixed ship adjustment are removed? Approach: we fitted 5-degree fields of 15 step sizes and a ship term against HadSST4.2 and ERSSTv5 (60S-60N, 1982-2025), smoothed them (1000 km) and tested the corrected record against ESA SST CCI v3, which the fit did not use. We then repeated the Terhaar et al. (2025, Nature) 2023/24 record-jump analysis and Hobday MHW statistics on 29,129 one-degree cells. Results: against CCI the DOISST warming excess falls from 0.044 to 0.002 C per decade and the 2020 step from +0.069 to -0.012 C. We reproduced the published jump (0.249 C over 2015/16) and end trend (0.269 C per decade) exactly. Homogenised DOISST gives a jump of 0.193 C (variants 0.187-0.200) and an end trend of 0.215; the 7 July 2020 step alone adds 0.080 C to the published jump. With the same AR(1) model, the mean return period falls from 435 years (published DOISST, our run; 512 published) to 130 years (110-155 for variants); ERSSTv5, HadSST4.2 and CCI give 138, 291 and 336 years. The jump stays unlikely but not unexpected, but the 1-in-512-year value is not robust. The 1982-2025 MHW-day trend falls from 21.2 to 15.7 days per decade (-26%), event frequency by 28% and cumulative intensity by 25%; CCI on the same cells lies between (16.1 against 18.6 and 13.5 for 1982-2023), so the steps cause 13-27% of the trend. 2023 MHW days fall from 125 to 103 per cell (CCI 114) and heatwave area from 96.9% to 94.7%, but 2023 stays a record and 2024 has more MHW days. The 2020 step enters over 3 days (4-8 July) with no change in the error field, which agrees with a satellite input change. Limitations: the in situ references share ships and drifters with DOISST, CCI has its own steps, and the jump correction differs by reference (CCI suggests 0.016 C, in situ fits 0.057 C on open water); the return period is very sensitive to the jump.
